title: fix(plugin-approvals): inbox search finds a request by the title, process label, object label and requester its row shows
body:
<!-- claude-projects-attribution: {"github_login":"os-support-ai"} -->
_Requested by **Yibo Wang** · [project thread](https://claude.ai/code/project/chan_01BVUyyPie8gHwoPM18iABwB?thread=cmsg_01BVUyyPie8gHwoPM18iABwBTDAJKyXUan6fJCKsZUf5Pv)_

Fixes #36959

Clause-②: no — the `q` parameter's accept set is unchanged; what it matches widens to the labels the row already shows the same caller.
Metadata-protocol: none — nothing an author writes changes.

## 维护者速读

- 审批人在审批收件箱的搜索框里输入列表上看到的文字(记录标题、流程名称、申请人姓名、对象名称),以前一条都搜不到,现在能搜到对应的申请。
- 属于审批收件箱的体验修复,替每天要在长队列里找申请的审批人解决「搜索框看起来是坏的」的问题。
- 出错时最坏情况是某个名称仍然搜不到(只会少搜,不会搜出调用者本来看不到的内容);纯服务端改动,撤回这次合并即可恢复原状。
- 无。

## What changes

`ApprovalService.buildRequestWhere` (`packages/plugins/plugin-approvals/src/approval-service.ts`) now adds served-text arms to the free-text `$or`, beside the four machine-column arms and the gated snapshot arm (both unchanged). A new `servedTextArms` works out the labels first, as this caller is served them, and turns each one into the machine values that name it:

- **process label**: for a flow where `readerLabels` picks a translation for the reader, `process_name IN` the flows whose picked label holds the term. For the other flows, `process_label` (the stored column, which is what those rows serve) holds the term AND `process_name IN` those flows. So a reader who is shown a translation is never found by the stored text they are not shown.
- **object label**: `readerLabels`' pick, else the schema label (the same pair `object_label` is set from), giving `object_name IN`.
- **requester name**: `resolveUserNames` (the resolver behind `submitter_name`) over the scope's submitters, giving `submitter_id IN`.
- **record title**: `recordsTitledWith`, per subject object, giving `object_name = O AND record_id IN`. The title is the shared `titleAsServed` over the caller's served fields from `servedFields`, which is the same `resolveReadableSnapshotFields` answer, asked as the caller, that `redactPayloads` and the served `record_title` use. With a schema, the driver read is first narrowed to records where a served title field holds the term; the served title still decides. `pickTitle`'s candidate list is now one shared `titleCandidates`.

The flows, objects, records and submitters to resolve come from one read of the requests under the query's own non-text filter (tenant, object, record, submitter, status; status is now set before the arms), newest first, capped at 5,000 with a `warn` when the cap is hit. Every arm carries a non-empty set. Anything that cannot be resolved adds no arm, so a failure narrows the search and never widens it. `freeTextMayMatchSnapshot` and its narrowing are unchanged. Matching stays case-sensitive (`$contains`), like the existing arms.

The placeholder ("Search record, process, requester…") is now accurate, so `ApprovalsInboxPage.tsx` and the i18n packs are untouched.

Read first (by risk):
1. `approval-service.ts`, `servedTextArms`: the process-label split (picked flows vs. the stored column narrowed to unpicked flows) is where the invariant could leak.
2. `approval-service.ts`, `recordsTitledWith`: the candidate filter by served fields and the `titleAsServed` post-filter.
3. `approval-inbox-search-display-text.integration.test.ts`: the "a term the caller is not served finds nothing" block.

Two-minute check: `pnpm --filter @objectstack/plugin-approvals exec vitest run --maxWorkers=2 src/approval-inbox-search-display-text.integration.test.ts`. Expect 21 tests to pass.

## Tests

New `src/approval-inbox-search-display-text.integration.test.ts` runs the real `ApprovalService` on a real `ObjectQL` over `SqlDriver` (better-sqlite3, in-memory, real DDL), in the filer's shape: security wired (so the snapshot arm is dropped) and an approver who can read every field. It covers:

- each of the filer's terms finds its row: titles (`Polar`, `Cargo`, `上海`, `拜访`, `UI测试`), process labels (`大额`, `出差申请审批`), requester names (`Dev`, `Admin`, `Sam Submitter`) and the object label (`商机`). Also checked with the object filter set, and `countRequests` agrees;
- machine-name control: `crm_` still finds every row and `large_opportunity` finds its row. With no field-visibility source wired, titles still match through the snapshot arm;
- visibility pins: a title field the caller may not read, or reads masked, finds nothing (the control with the field readable does). A zh-CN reader who is served the translated process label is found by the translation and not by the stored label; a reader with no locale gets the reverse.

`approval-free-text-scope.test.ts`: the expected column sets now include `process_label`, and the "never empty" arm count goes from 4 to 5. Its four properties are unchanged.

<details><summary>Red on main (the service at the base commit, the new test file)</summary>

`git restore --source=0212714711 -- approval-service.ts` (count of `servedTextArms` 5 to 0), then the file: `Tests 16 failed | 5 passed (21)`. Every filer term failed (titles, process labels, requester names, object label, object-filtered, count, the readable control and the translated-label case). The five that passed are the fixture-serves check, the two machine controls, the unwired-titles check and the masked-title pin, which passes on main only because nothing matched. Restored with `git checkout HEAD --`: `git diff HEAD` empty, blob equals HEAD.

</details>

<details><summary>Ablations (scripts/ablation-replace.mjs, restore verified by blob == HEAD and an empty diff)</summary>

- Title arm ignores the caller's served fields (`recordsTitledWith(object, ids, undefined, q)`), anchor 1 to 0: `Tests 2 failed | 19 passed`. The failures are both masked-title pins.
- Stored process label no longer narrowed to unpicked flows (`arms.push({ process_label: { $contains: q } })`), anchor 1 to 0: `Tests 1 failed | 20 passed`. The failure is the translated-label pin.

The subject is imported from source (`./approval-service.js`), so no `dist/` leg applies.

</details>

## Acceptance notes

- Case: matching stays case-sensitive (`$contains` is case-exact on every backend), so `polar` does not find `Polar Cargo`, which matches the existing machine arms. A case-insensitive search would be its own change (`$icontains` is ASCII-only).
- A record title that comes only from a deleted record's snapshot is not searched by the new path; in an unwired deployment the snapshot arm still covers it.
- A row whose stored `process_label` is blank serves a fallback label (the config snapshot or a prettified machine name) that is not searched. The display-label backfill fills that column at boot.
- Cost: each search with a term adds one bounded scope read (5,000 rows, three machine columns), one `sys_user` read for the scope's submitters, and one title read per subject object in scope.
